feature: Pi-owned SDK parent-session compaction with validated native-context handoff

ownership.summarizer: Pi default compaction pipeline through the selected provider
ownership.oldNativeContext: closed after Pi persists compaction and the SDK receipt
ownership.newNativeContext: summary and retained Pi messages as labeled JSON data, never executable historical calls
ownership.newTools: unchanged Pi schemas, validation, permissions and execution

red.fixture: real Pi RPC/default compactor and provider; external SDK replay only

replayE2E.checkpointGap: Owned RPC worker SIGKILL after durable receipt, before its first post-compaction SDK response; marker recall then succeeded after restart
replayE2E.receiptGap: Controlled truncation before receipt publication; continuation rejected without another SDK request. This is not a power-loss/partial-filesystem-write proof.
assertions: Every new call has its real Pi result; counted effects never replay
Unmatched calls and unknown SDK work cannot be hidden by compaction, including while another provider is selected
Source, summary/projection, instructions and receipt corruption reject before SDK startup
Summary errors and Stop leave prior history usable
Queued notice order survives the compaction boundary
Tool activation at the automatic boundary and activation/Stop after compaction work
Summary usage remains in Pi session totals

liveManual.fixture: real models, normal personal/project resources, Pi RPC, isolated host and mobile Chromium; no model mocks or credential copies

liveAutomatic.fixture: same real provider contract with bounded inert padding reads and a project-local 45K threshold
liveAutomatic.partialTurnSummary: For SDK runs, the first between-tool summary did not itself contain the marker because the matching tool batch/result was retained. The subsequent summary contained it; no-tool recall and restart then passed.

liveAssertions: Marker obtained through a real read, not supplied in the user prompt
Acknowledgements omit the marker so retained ACK text cannot satisfy recall
A generated summary actually retains the marker
Recall without additional tools before and after replacing only the owned worker
Original audit bytes retained and tool-call/result IDs match
Personal settings unchanged and owned parent workers closed

retainedFailures.finding: The replay peer wrongly required a marker in every split-summary request; a pending-user prefix need not contain it. Fixture corrected to require it in the relevant history, not invent it in every prefix.
Repeated identical summaries made Pi's event identify an older compaction entry. The adapter now binds the latest persisted entry and checks the event's summary.

First live automatic Haiku recall refused to reveal the marker because the earlier no-print acknowledgement instruction sounded permanent. The latest summary did retain the value. Clarified one-turn output restrictions and explicit later authorization passed on all three models; this was not another ACK_0 summary loss.

notVerified: Borrowed foreground-worker compaction without provider-local hooks
Power loss, partial filesystem writes or every publication crash boundary
Sonnet live compaction and other full provider journeys in this change
Lossless retention of all historical details
privacy: Artifacts are local temporary-directory basenames. Raw system prompts, browser traces, sessions, native transcripts and tool payloads remain private.
